title: Chronicle probe enricher and incident priority scorer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Why: Our current alert surface produces noisy pages during multi-region microbursts and misses cross-signal incidents where traces, logs, and metrics point to the same user-impacting failure. Goal: build an enriched probe and scoring pipeline (Chronicle) that stitches traces/logs/metrics, computes an incident priority score, and emits a single deduplicated alert with metadata for routing and severity decisions.

Scope:
- Probe hydration: enrich synthetic and sampled traces with log excerpts, metric deltas, and customer tags.
- Span fingerprinting: compute canonical signatures for span groups to identify recurring root causes.
- Incident priority scorer: combine SLO burn-rate, estimated affected user count, error class entropy, customer tier, and regional impact into a single 0-100 score.
- Alert output: emit structured alerts to Pager (with priority mapping), Console dashboards, and the incident datastore.
- Quiet-hours & fatigue weighting: apply suppression heuristics and on-call fatigue decay to avoid overpaging.

Out of scope: persistent storage changes to the primary event store (we'll use a shadow store in Chronicle for trial).
acceptance_criteria: Chronicle pipeline deployed to staging and receives synthetic probes and 10% trace traffic
Incident priority score correlates with manual severity labels in 95% of sampled historical incidents (benchmarked on last 6 months)
False-positive pages reduced by >=30% for noise-heavy endpoints compared to baseline
Alerts include structured fields: incident_score, top_spans, affected_customers, suggested_route, and root_cause_hint
On-call paging policy honors quiet-hours suppression and includes fatigue-adjusted severity mapping
implementation_notes: Pipeline will be implemented as a new k8s service (chronicle-enricher) consuming OTLP and log-bridge topics
Span fingerprinting uses a canonicalization step + Murmur3 hash to create stable keys; compare against a lightweight redis-backed cache for recent signatures
Anomaly detector: hybrid approach combining seasonal-trend decomposition for metrics and an isolation-forest model for residual outliers
Scoring model: linear weighted model initially (weights configurable in Console), with telemetry to compare against a later ML ranking model
Backpressure: chronicle-enricher should gracefully drop enrichment for low-priority traces and record sampling decisions in trace metadata
Privacy: PII redaction runs as a pipeline filter before enrichment; ensure KMS integration for any persisted snippets
test_plan: Unit tests for span canonicalization and fingerprint stability
Integration test that stitches a trace with 3 logs and verifies fields appear in enriched output
Synthetic incident replay: run 200 historical incidents through Chronicle in staging and validate score distribution
Chaos test: simulate burst of 10k traces/min to validate throttling and no pages during graceful degradation
A/B experiment: route 50% of pages for a noisy endpoint through Chronicle scoring and measure on-call noise and time-to-ack
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy chronicle-enricher -> validate on synthetic probes (1 day)
Phase 2 (canary): 10% production traffic + 1 smaller customer org -> monitor false positives and score calibration (3 days)
Phase 3 (regional ramp): enable for a single region with full paging enabled for high-severity scores (7 days)
Phase 4 (global): flip rollout with fallback toggle; schedule playbook review with support and SRE (2 days)
Emergency rollback path: feature flag that routes processed alerts back to legacy aggregator
